bounded_statement: The selected result's inferential claim (two-sample Student t test, t(16) = 19.600, p < 0.001, on all 18 readings) is not supported at the stated level: the declared independent unit is plot_id, there are only 6 plots (3 rewetted, 3 drained), and each plot's 3 repeat-visit rows were entered as separate independent observations into ttest_ind, inflating the effective sample size from 6 to 18 and the degrees of freedom from 4 to 16. The issue is bounded to the validity of the stated test statistic, df, and p-value; the direction and approximate magnitude of the treatment difference are not in dispute (plot-level aggregation to one mean per plot still yields roughly t(4) ~ 10.0, p ~ 0.0006).

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the repeated-measures structure (6 plots each visited 3 rounds) and that every reading entered the test separately, so the analysis is not concealed; and the underlying effect is robust: per-plot means are cleanly separated between treatments (rewetted plot means ~18.7, 21.5, 20.1 vs drained ~7.9, 9.6, 6.5), so a correctly aggregated plot-level t test (n = 3 per group) would still reject the null (approximately t(4) = 10.0, p ~ 0.0006). This mitigates the practical impact on the directional conclusion but does not validate the stated t(16) statistic or p-value.

[selected-result] Mean chamber methane flux was higher under rewetting than under drainage (20.10 vs 8.00 mg m-2 h-1; difference 12.10 mg m-2 h-1), two-sample Student t test on all 18 readings, t(16) = 19.600, p < 0.001.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the finding three ways. (1) Checked whether the workflow performs any per-plot aggregation, mixed modelling, or cluster-robust adjustment before the test: it does not; fluxes_for filters rows only by treatment and ttest_ind receives all 9 row-level readings per group, with dof computed as 9+9-2=16. (2) Checked whether rows might actually be independent despite reappearing plot_ids: the data description explicitly rules this out, naming plot_id as the independent unit and stating that rows sharing a plot_id are repeat visits to one collar whose readings resemble each other; the CSV confirms every plot_id appears exactly three times. (3) Verified the reported numbers are what the pseudoreplicated procedure would produce, to exclude a mere reporting error: group means 20.10 and 8.00, SDs 1.240 and 1.376, and pooled-variance t = 12.10 / sqrt(((1.240^2 + 1.376^2)/2) * (2/9)) = 19.60 with df 16 all reproduce exactly, confirming the t(16) statistic derives from treating 18 non-independent rows as 18 independent observations. All three checks failed to falsify; the issue stands.

root_cause: The workflow extracts all rows for each treatment (fluxes_for filters only on the treatment column, ignoring plot_id) and passes the full row-level vectors of 9 readings per group to scipy.stats.ttest_ind with dof = len(wet) + len(dry) - 2 = 16. Because each of the 6 plots contributes 3 repeat visits to the same permanent collar, and the description states readings from the same collar tend to resemble each other, the same independent unit enters the row-independent t procedure three times, violating its independence assumption and understating the standard error / overstating the degrees of freedom.
